summary: An LTP subscription: Vortex's 22-byte ltp packet carries no time, so both frames are stamped on receipt; a heartbeat frame and a text order postback reach nobody; after the unsubscribe the ticker is taken back at its mode.

notes: The query carries auth_token, no login frame (rupeezy_websocket.py, module docstring).

deviations.reason: data.mode is the label every broker's frames carry on the desktop (ltp, quote, full), as the recorded Zerodha transcripts carry it; the Rupeezy web adapter sends no data.mode.

The Rupeezy web adapter adds the broker's instrument token as a string to every frame; the desktop's common carrier has no place for it. Whether the desktop carries it is the lead's decision (a broker identifier, not a market field).
The Rupeezy web adapter repeats ltp as last_price in every frame; the desktop sends no such alias yet.

An ltp packet, or an ohlcv packet with no trade time, carries no trade time; the web sends ltt null, the desktop sends the receipt time as the trade time (the bridge's fallback), which the lead's rules forbid. A desktop defect: mark the trade time absent for such packets, so ltt is left out (the desktop's form of null).
deviations.ref: rupeezy_adapter.py:222 (ltt None without a trade time); feed::bridge::ltt; BKD-03

deviations.reason: Without a trade time or update time the web sends timestamp null, a market data frame with no time (the SDK reads data.timestamp); the desktop stamps the time the packet was received.
deviations.ref: rupeezy_adapter.py:223 ((last_update_time or ltt or 0) * 1000 or None)
